The Chief of the General Staff, General Nikolai Ogarkov, a hard-headed officer of the old school, reacted angrily.

paragraphs.source_en: Ustinov is reported to have asked late in 1979: “If [they can] do all these preparations under our noses, why should we hunker down, play cautious and lose Afghanistan?”44 At a Politburo meeting on 12 December, Ustinov, alongside a clutch of grey old men like Leonid Brezhnev, Andrei Gromyko, Yuri Andropov and Konstantin Chernenko, gave the go-ahead for a full-blown deployment of troops in Afghanistan.45 It had not been a simple decision to take, Brezhnev was quoted as saying in Pravda a few weeks later.46 A fortnight after the meeting, on Christmas Eve 1979, Soviet forces began to stream over the border as part of Operation Storm 333.
